Author: gustav-mango-unique-ai
Message:
feat: add applications layer (ArgoCD, Helm apps, instance config) (#7)

## Summary

Adds the applications layer (06-applications) — a forkable ArgoCD-driven
deployment template for AWS EKS. The `main` branch carries
`<PLACEHOLDER>` tokens; deployment branches substitute real values via
`configure-instance.sh`.

### Applications

- **12 system apps**: ArgoCD, cert-manager, external-secrets, Kong,
storage-class, reloader, Elasticsearch, ECK, RabbitMQ operator, Zitadel,
AWS LB controller, KEDA
- **21 chat apps**: backend services, AI services, web apps, RabbitMQ,
Qdrant, LiteLLM
- **LiteLLM proxy**: Bedrock model routing — EU cross-region inference
(Claude), application inference profile (Cohere Embed v4)
- **Kong ingress**: ClusterIP proxy with TargetGroupBindings — AWS LB
Controller registers pods into Terraform-managed NLB target groups

### Instance configuration tooling

- `configure-instance.sh` — idempotent placeholder replacement with
state tracking
- `validate-instance.sh` — ensures no placeholder tokens remain after
configuration
- `validate.sh` — YAML lint, shellcheck, value file reference integrity,
secret scanning

### Cross-layer changes

Changes to layers 02–05 discovered during sbx deployment and review:

- **03-infrastructure**: Restore `resolve_aws_region()` function and
subshell `cd` pattern in `connect-ssm.sh`; restore
`local.secondary_cidr`; fix variable renames (`enable_*` prefix); harden
NLB ingress with SG-scoped rules and secondary CIDR egress; add S3 VPC
endpoint policy allowance
- **05-compute**: Add launch template to attach `eks_nodes` SG to
managed node groups (encrypted gp3, IMDSv2); migrate inline SG rules to
standalone resources; add EBS CSI KMS permissions, ingress NLB→EKS SG
rule, Quay pull-through cache, node group alignment, IAM policy refactor
(native HCL data sources)
- **04-data-and-ai**: Aurora final snapshot identifier, Bedrock resource
rename, S3 random suffix, restrict Aurora/ElastiCache SG to private
subnets
- **02-governance**: Remove redundant `tags = local.tags` (already in
`default_tags`)
- **All terraform layers**: Remove `merge(local.tags, ...)` —
`default_tags` in providers.tf handles base tags; resources carry only
resource-specific tags

### Security baseline

All scanner suppressions documented in
[`docs/security-baseline.md`](docs/security-baseline.md) with rationale,
compensating controls, and production remediation notes. New entries:

- `CKV_AWS_341` — IMDS hop limit 2 required for EKS containerized
workloads
- `CKV_AWS_24/25/260` — checkov false positive on
`referenced_security_group_id`
([checkov#6624](https://github.com/bridgecrewio/checkov/issues/6624))
- `allowInsecureImages` — Bitnami legacy RabbitMQ operator images are
unsigned

### Validation

`scripts/validate.sh all <env> true` now validates all layers in a
single command (terraform fmt, tflint, shellcheck, trivy, checkov for
layers 01–05; yamllint, shellcheck, refs, secrets for 06-applications).

## Test plan

- [x] All 33 ArgoCD apps Synced/Healthy on sbx
- [x] `terraform plan` clean on layers 03–05 against sbx
- [x] `./scripts/validate.sh all sbx true` — all layers pass
- [x] `06-applications/scripts/validate.sh sbx` — YAML, shellcheck,
refs, secrets all pass
- [x] Cherry-pick gap scan: all structural changes synced between deploy
and template branches
- [x] PR 2–6 review comment audit — no regressions

Author: gustav-mango-unique-ai
Message:
feat: root-level scaffolding for AWS workload account template (#1)

## Summary

- Add `.gitignore` for Terraform state, plans, and local working
directories
- Add `common.auto.tfvars.template` for cross-layer configuration with
naming convention guidance
- Add `modules/naming/` — centralized naming and tagging module with AWS
length constraints
- Add deployment, validation, and operational scripts (deploy, destroy,
validate, secret scanning, KMS/Secrets Manager recovery)
- Add `scripts/gitleaks-config.toml` with per-rule allowlists for false
positive suppression
- Overwrite `README.md` with full architecture documentation: 6-layer
structure, platform topologies, naming conventions, validation
toolchain, and cross-layer dependency model

## Context

First PR in a stacked branch train (`feat/00-root` → `feat/01-bootstrap`
→ ... → `feat/06-applications`) to turn this repo into a forkable
reference architecture for AWS workload accounts.

This PR establishes the root-level foundation. No AWS resources are
created — actual infrastructure begins in `feat/01-bootstrap`.

## Validation

- [x] `gitleaks` — 6 commits scanned, no leaks found
- [x] `checkov` — no findings (naming module has no checkable resources)
- [x] `shellcheck` — all scripts pass clean
- [x] All account-specific values scrubbed (placeholder conventions
documented)
